question.text: On premature exit from NPS Tier 1 before age 60, and assuming the accumulated pension wealth exceeds INR 5 lakhs, what percentage of the accumulated corpus must be used to purchase an annuity?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B, the general rule for premature exit from NPS Tier 1 (before age 60 or before superannuation/retirement) is that at least 80% of the accumulated pension wealth must be used to purchase an annuity from an empanelled insurance company, and the balance is paid out as a lump sum. This 80% threshold is more restrictive than the requirement that applies at normal retirement. The Trap: Candidates often carry over the normal-retirement figure of 40% and apply it to premature exit. The question specifically asks about premature exit, where the mandatory annuitisation requirement is significantly higher at 80%. Note: There is an exception to this general rule: if the accumulated pension wealth at exit is equal to or less than INR 5 lakhs, the subscriber may withdraw the entire amount, so the 80% rule applies only when the corpus exceeds that threshold.
